span.term: implicit control cues must leave a memory trace that survives across trials, and only consciously represented events are strong enough to bridge that interval, so unconscious implicit cues never reach the control system

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: adapting to a statistical property such as conflict frequency requires accumulating information across many separate episodes over a long period, an accumulation that unconscious representations cannot support

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: control is executed by if-then plans; explicit cues let participants specify both sides of the plan in advance, whereas implicit events leave the if-side and then-side vague, so the plan itself has to be revised and it is this revision that demands awareness
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The proposed resolution: control cued by a single explicit signal can be triggered without awareness, while control that has to be inferred from a pattern of events cannot
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: An implicit cue is one where the environment never signals the need for control - it merely suggests it, so the actor must infer it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Unconscious stimuli are processed only where the system was prepared in advance to process them, so preparation rather than awareness does the work
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Conflict adaptation works by reallocating attention toward the relevant stimulus aspects after conflict is frequent or recent

span.label: An indirect route could fake unconscious control: the prime stays unconscious while its behavioural consequences do not, and the actor adjusts to those

span.label: critiques → Dehaene and Naccache's workspace model, which reserves cognitive control for consciousness
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHICH PROCESSES NEED CONSCIOUSNESS. 'DEHAENE AND NACCACHE (2001) SUGGEST IN THEIR WORKSPACE MODEL THAT ROUTINE ACTIONS ARE POSSIBLE WITHOUT CONSCIOUSNESS, WHILE CONSCIOUSNESS IS REQUIRED FOR COGNITIVE CONTROL.' The model is stated precisely enough to be tested and the critique targets exactly the line it draws - so the disagreement is about WHERE the boundary falls, not whether there is one. Q-505.

span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS AN ASSUMED PRECONDITION. 'Quotation withheld.' Unconscious processing is granted only where the system was set up for it, so a null in an unprepared condition is not evidence against unconscious processing - it is outside the claim. Q-511.

The span: 'in studies on task switching, participants have to respond to the same stimuli in a different way depending on the currently instructed task context, and thus Quotation withheld'. The sentence says CONTROL IS INVOLVED IN SWITCHING - the paradigm engages the faculty. The edge says the paradigm is a component of the faculty, which is the other way round; and `is believed` marks it as the field's view rather than this paper's finding. span.label: When the need for control is signalled by a single explicit cue, that cue does not have to be consciously perceived for control to be recruited.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: When the need for control is only implied by recent or frequent response conflict, awareness of that event appears to be necessary, and unconscious induction of control is not reliably obtained.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Exactly three control functions have so far been shown to be triggerable by subliminal explicit cues: task preparation, response inhibition, and orienting of attention.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Masked primes reliably activate task sets, facilitating the cued task and even biasing which task is freely chosen.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Strategic adaptation to how often conflict occurs is obtained only when the conflicting irrelevant information is consciously seen.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Conflict adaptation requires that the prime in the preceding trial was visible, yet the control settings so established still act on masked primes in the current trial - so awareness is needed to invoke control, not to execute it.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Context-specific proportion-congruency adaptation appeared with visible primes but disappeared with subliminal primes, whose overall congruency effect was unaffected by the context cue.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Taken as a whole the literature is inconsistent: some experiments show control prompted by unnoticed events and others show it fails.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The authors argue that cognitive control itself does not depend on the actor having meta-knowledge about when or how control is being applied.
